findings.finding: The JonesTrading Capital on Demand ATM (S-3 effective 2026-05-12/13, upsized by $9.69m on 2026-07-17) is open and can sell into any bounce on 2026-09-25. The issuer carries going-concern language, raised about $11.0m through the ATM in July, and has shown it will draw.
findings.mechanism_in_window: The ATM is a standing daily seller with no pricing event. It can be drawn in the 09-25 session with nothing to file until the next 10-Q, so the supply lands inside the window whether or not anyone can see it. Its capacity is limited by the baby-shelf cap (one-third of public float at the 60-day high, net of sales over the prior 12 months), and remaining room is not disclosed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July 2026 draw window is the comparable. The 2026-07-09 fall (-24.0%) was followed by -13.68% the next session and +0.91% after that; the 424B5 upsizing landed 2026-07-17 (baseline history; 8-K of 2026-07-17). Shares outstanding went from about 9.4m (Q2 weighted basic) to 13.34m by 2026-08-11, so the ATM has already added about 40% to the count.
findings.why_not_priced: The close prices the known overhang only as a level. It does not price a seller that takes the other side of every uptick next session, which caps a reflexive bounce from a two-day, -34% slide into $1.07. If the market held this, the 09-25 session would show a failed open-to-close bounce rather than a sustained recovery. Market cap at spot is about $14m against cash of $15.8m at 06-30 plus July ATM proceeds, which is exactly the setup where management keeps drawing.
